description:
Stations get levels. A level widens the catchment area, or cuts pollution, noise or upkeep. You buy levels in the station's window, one at a time or all you can in one click, and can remove them again.

HOW IT WORKS
- Open a station and expand its Retrofit card. Collapsed, the card shows one row per retrofit: 15 level boxes (white: bought, grey: open to your rank, dark: needs a higher rank) and what the levels do now. Expanded, each row shows what the next level changes, the upkeep after it, and three buttons: < removes the top level for 80% of what it costs today, > buys the next level, >| buys every level your rank and money allow (for the same total as one by one). Hover over a row for the prices.
- Levels cost money. A retrofit's highest level is your company rank, up to 15. The buy buttons are greyed out when the next level needs a higher rank or you do not have enough money for it, and the row's tooltip says which. If your money drops below the price just as you click, the level is not bought, nothing is charged, and a yellow note says "Not bought: not enough money" until you have the money again (at least 10 seconds).
- Buying or removing a level rebuilds the station. Waiting passengers stay. When something built after the station stands in the way, such as a town building or a road rebuilt next to it, the game cannot rebuild the station: the level is not bought (or not removed), nothing is charged or given back, and a yellow "Not rebuilt" banner shows on the card. Clear what is in the way and click again.
- The game's own rebuilds keep the levels, for example adding, moving or removing modules with Configure.
- A removed level gives back 80% of what it would cost to buy now, not of what you paid, so a level bought long ago can give back more than it cost. Levels are saved with the game.

THE FOUR RETROFITS
- Catchment radius: every catchment circle of the station grows by 3% per level, or at least 5 m (+45% or at least +75 m at level 15).
- Pollution: -5% per level (-75% at level 15).
- Noise: -5% per level (-75% at level 15).
- Upkeep: -5% of the total upkeep per level (-75% at level 15).
- Harbours get only the catchment and upkeep retrofits: a harbour gives off no pollution or noise of its own.
- Pollution and noise levels lower only what the station itself gives off. Vehicles and tracks keep their own pollution and noise.
- The town window shows the effect best: the list of pollution sources and the Pollution Rating graph on a town's pollution card. Expect a real but small change: industries, company vehicles and tracks give off much of a town's pollution, and the mod does not change them. In a test, pollution level 9 on all 16 stations of a town cut the town's pollution by about 11%, and its rating stayed Poor.

COSTS
- Level 1 costs 20% of what the station would cost to build today in the catchment retrofit (4% in pollution, 8% in noise, 16% in upkeep), and each level after that costs more than the one before: 15% more in catchment and upkeep, 12% in noise, 10% in pollution. A harbour's upkeep retrofit costs half.
- Each catchment level adds 15% of the station's normal upkeep, each noise level 10% and each pollution level 5%. The upkeep retrofit cuts the total upkeep by 5% per level. With the other three retrofits at 15, a full upkeep retrofit pays for itself in about 11 game years (a harbour with full catchment: about 9).
- A station's build price includes its modules, so the levels of a large station cost more. Modules added later raise the price of the next levels, and the upkeep the levels add grows with them.

WHICH STATIONS
- The game's train stations, road and tram stations and harbours, for passengers and cargo, including ones built before the mod was added. A newly placed station starts at level 0 in every retrofit.
- Not covered: airports, airfields and heliports, the underground station, kerbside bus and tram stops, and stations from other mods that bring their own construction file.

NOT CHECKED YET
- Whether changing a station's era or adding catenary keeps the levels.
- What a rebuild does to vehicles standing at the platforms and to waiting cargo.
- What happens to levelled stations when the mod is removed from a save. Keep a backup of any save you play with the mod.

COMPATIBILITY
- Depot Retrofits levels depots and maintenance buildings; the two mods do not touch each other's buildings.
- Works with TRM: Industry Emissions in either load order, and both mods' cuts to pollution and noise apply.
- With TRM: Infrastructure Upkeep, prices and refunds are lower by the share of upkeep it cuts, as they are worked out from the upkeep the game charges.
- The mod replaces no game script. It wraps each station's own build script: the station is built as the game builds it, and then the levels are applied.
- It contains no files from the game.

Source and notes: https://github.com/WuphonsReach/tf3-station-retrofits (MIT licence).
name: Station Retrofits
summary: Stations get levels for a wider catchment area, less pollution and noise, and lower upkeep.
